import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_58/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_58/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_58/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_58/test_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_58/test_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_58/test_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_58/test_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_58/test_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_58/test_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_58/test_9.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_58/test_10.csv"
]

# Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly ['code', 'name'] and types are consistent
    df = df[['code', 'name']].copy()
    # Convert 'code' to integer type explicitly
    df['code'] = df['code'].astype(int)
    # Convert 'name' to string type explicitly
    df['name'] = df['name'].astype(str)
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the same schema as the target,
# we can concatenate (union) all source tables directly.
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# The target examples show duplicates exist (e.g., multiple rows with same code and name),
# so we do NOT drop duplicates.

# Final target schema: ['code': integer, 'name': string]
# Already ensured by dtype conversions above.

# Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_58/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
